title: Private upgrade safepoint manager and migration strategy
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Private (VPC / on‑prem) customers run clusters with heterogeneous environments (K8s versions, custom storage drivers, strict network policy). Existing upgrade tooling applies migrations as a monolithic phase which has caused two customer incidents: long tenant blocking windows and unrecoverable schema mismatches when a node fails mid‑upgrade.

Goal: Implement a Safepoint Manager and migration orchestration design that makes upgrades resumable, observable, and reversible for Private deployments. The system should: (1) create lightweight safepoints that capture minimal cluster state and migration offset, (2) allow rolling application of migrations with per‑component checkpoints, (3) provide an auditable migration journal for air‑gapped installs, and (4) integrate with rollout gates (canary, LTS channel checks, auto‑fallback).

Scope and deliverables:
- Safepoint Manager service (stateless controller + persistent journal) with APIs to create, list, and restore safepoints.
- Migration runner that executes schema and operator changes in small reversible steps and updates the journal after each step.
- Canary rollout integration: preflight checks, incremental traffic reallocation, and automatic rollback triggers (latency/error/telemetry thresholds).
- Offline/journal export format for customers in air‑gapped environments (signed JSONL with checksums).
- Upgrade cutover playbooks for SRE and on‑prem partners and a test harness for simulating mid‑migration failure/restore.

Constraints and non‑goals:
- This ticket does not implement new DB migration DSL; it adapts existing migration scripts to be stepwise and idempotent.
- We will not redesign operator CRD schemas in this phase; we will add compatibility layers where necessary.
acceptance_criteria: Safepoint Manager exposes API to create/list/restore safepoints and persists a journal that survives controller restarts.
Migrations run as sequences of idempotent steps; each step records a completion entry in the journal.
Canary rollout integration toggles traffic and auto‑triggers rollback when telemetry thresholds crossed (latency > 200ms for 5m or error rate > 2%).
Air‑gapped export/import produces a signed JSONL migration journal and can be applied by offline operators to resume upgrades.
End‑to‑end test: simulate node failure mid‑migration and recover to a safepoint without data loss or manual DB surgery.
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Private PM, and Platform Infra. Agreed to prioritize resumability over full automation for initial rollout.
2026-03-05: Spike completed — proof of concept safepoint journal persisted to S3/GCS and to local file for air‑gapped. Found GC corner case with journal size; plan to snapshot periodic compaction.
2026-03-08: Design doc published: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Private+Safepoint+Manager+Design (internal). Added a section describing signed JSONL export for compliance teams.
2026-03-10: Wireframes for Console integration (Migration timeline view + safepoint list) uploaded: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/SAFEPOINT-WIREFRAMES
2026-03-11: Implementation started — core controller scaffolding up in repo. PR opened for journal schema and compacted storage: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1428
2026-03-13: Telemetry thresholds refined after SRE input. Added histogram buckets for pre/post upgrade token latency. Drafted rollback playbook and runbook snippets.
2026-03-14: Completed step runner interface and local simulator that can inject failures between steps. Next: integrate canary gating and signed export for air‑gapped.
comments: PM (Jordan Lee): We need clear messaging to customers on what a 'safepoint' means; add a glossary entry in the playbook.
SRE (Hannah Chen): Ensure journal persistence supports eventual consistency for object stores — add a vector clock or monotonic sequence so resumes are deterministic.
Design (Noah Patel): Console should show safepoint provenance (who/what created it) and allow rollback only with two‑person confirmation for enterprise installs.
Security (Lina Gomez): Signed offline journals must be HMAC‑protected and verifiable against customer KMS; file format draft attached to design doc.
notes: Tradeoffs discussed: optimistic step commit (fast) vs two‑phase commit (stronger correctness). We chose optimistic with compensating steps to keep latency low for customer clusters. Long term: evaluate a hybrid two‑phase commit for critical schema changes.
